## Choose a backend and model

Start with a provider you can access, check whether you need live or batch
processing, and configure only its credential. A model identifier is the exact
name sent to that service. Use its official catalog to check availability, then
try a small request with minimal controls before planning a larger run.

This page provides the backend/key table and dated test evidence. A past success
is useful evidence about one configuration, not a recommendation or a promise
that it remains available. See [Getting Started](getting-started.html) for a first
request and [Provider Controls and Recovery](provider-controls-and-recovery.html)
for troubleshooting.

## What the package supports

`pairwiseLLM` implements request and response handling for seven backends. The
package generally forwards `model` identifiers to the selected provider; it
does not maintain an exhaustive model allowlist.

| Backend | Provider surface | Live | Batch | Credential |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `openai` | OpenAI generative endpoints; opt-in Decisions | yes | generative only | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `anthropic` | Anthropic | yes | yes | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `gemini` | Gemini Developer API | yes | yes | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| `vertex` | Vertex AI Gemini API | yes | no | `VERTEX_API_KEY` |
| `together` | Together AI | yes | no | `TOGETHER_API_KEY` |
| `typesafe` | TypeSafe Jev (`systemone`) | yes | no | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` |
| `ollama` | Local Ollama server | yes | no | none |

Backend implementation is not the same as compatibility with every model.
Endpoint compatibility depends on the request shape a model accepts;
maintainer testing covers only the exact configurations below; and current
availability is controlled by the provider. Preview identifiers and reasoning
controls can change independently of this package.

Check current availability in the official catalogs for
[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all),
[Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview),
[Gemini Developer API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models),
[Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/model-versions),
and [Together AI](https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/models).
[TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) documents Jev versions and aliases.
Ollama tags depend on what is installed on the local server.

## Dated compatibility record

The machine-readable source is installed at
`inst/extdata/model_compatibility.csv`. Absence from this registry does not
imply incompatibility. A `true` value records a successful maintained smoke
test for that exact mode; a live success is not evidence of batch success.
The dated detailed result artifacts are
`inst/extdata/model_smoke_results_2026-09-05.csv` and
`inst/extdata/model_batch_smoke_results_2026-09-05.csv`. The October 16 decision qualification is summarized below and in the registry;
its private raw journals are not distributed. Standard generative configurations
omit `temperature` and `top_p`, so their model/provider defaults apply.

```{r registry}
registry_path <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "model_compatibility.csv",
  package = "pairwiseLLM"
)
if (!nzchar(registry_path)) {
  source_paths <- c(
    file.path("inst", "extdata", "model_compatibility.csv"),
    file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "model_compatibility.csv")
  )
  registry_path <- source_paths[file.exists(source_paths)][1]
}
registry <- utils::read.csv(registry_path, check.names = FALSE)
registry[c(
  "backend", "model_id", "endpoint", "live_tested", "batch_tested",
  "reasoning_mode", "package_version", "test_date", "status"
)]
```

Registry statuses mean:

- `tested-current`: the recorded configuration passed on the stated date and
  was current in the provider catalog when checked.
- `tested-legacy`: a successful dated test whose identifier is now legacy.
- `retired`: the provider has retired the identifier; it is retained only as
  historical evidence.
- `unverified`: availability or a partial response was observed, but no
  successful parsed package result was established.

### Optional future checks

The opt-in `inst/scripts/smoke_model_compatibility.R` harness can re-test
selected live or batch configurations and write a dated result artifact. It
makes billable network calls and is intentionally excluded from the package
test suite. For example:

```text
PAIRWISELLM_RUN_PROVIDER_SMOKE=true \
  Rscript inst/scripts/smoke_model_compatibility.R \
  --mode=live --providers=openai,anthropic
```

Selected providers must have their recorded API-key environment variables set;
otherwise the harness records `skipped-no-key` and exits unsuccessfully. Use
`--allow-missing-keys=true` only when those skipped rows are intentional.

Claude 5 reasoning is not advertised here: that family uses adaptive-thinking
semantics that this package does not currently implement and test. Likewise,
Ollama names such as `qwen3:32b`, `gemma3:27b`, and
`mistral-small3.2:24b` are only dated, environment-dependent local examples,
not claims about what another Ollama installation provides.

## Decision-model live qualification

On **2026-10-16**, an owner-authorized live smoke run used pairwiseLLM 1.6.0,
PR #343 HEAD `8a220cb2a6ebdf55faed4d1712ce4e23c2b2dd79`:

| Provider | Exact requested model | Live endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `gpt-6-luna` | `decisions` (`POST /v1/decisions`) |
| TypeSafe | `jev-1.13.0` | `systemone` (`POST /v1/systemone`) |

Both used the bundled **20 synthetic writing samples**, Overall Quality, the
same **60 primary pairs** (each item appeared in six pairs), and **10 reversed
presentation audits per provider**, plus a separate single-pair preflight for
each. No provider-managed Batch jobs were used. Both preflights succeeded;
both providers returned 60/60 valid primary decisions and all 10 reverse audits.
All 120 primary SAMPLE_1 probabilities were finite and within [0,1], selected
winners agreed with their probabilities and belonged to their submitted pairs,
and all 20 items had finite Firth-adjusted BT estimates for each provider.

Primary winners agreed on 53/60 pairs (88.33%; kappa 0.7619). The two sets of BT
scores had Pearson correlation 0.9211 and Spearman correlation 0.9053. Winner
agreement under reversed presentation was 7/10 for OpenAI and 5/10 for TypeSafe.
These are descriptive results from a small synthetic pilot. The reversal
results raise a position-consistency concern for further study; they do not
establish an implementation defect or that the providers are interchangeable.
Provider probabilities have not been shown to be calibrated, and this run does
not validate educational scoring or replace BT inference.

The live evidence establishes compatibility and end-to-end completion for these
configurations on that date. Its aggregate summaries do not establish exact
transmission counts, every outbound JSON field, interruption/retry behavior,
lock exclusion, or zero new sends on restart. Those implementation paths are
qualified separately with provider-free regression tests. OpenAI Decisions
currently accepts only `gpt-6-luna` in this package. Other Jev versions and the
moving `jev-latest`/`jev-preview` aliases are accepted but were not tested here;
record requested and reported model versions, and do not assume aliases freeze
model weights or future availability.

### Reproduce the design without sharing private data

Prepare the bundled samples locally, select a connected degree-six graph with
60 unique primary pairs, freeze the same oriented pair table for both providers,
and select 10 of those pairs for reversed audits with distinct occurrence IDs.
Use Overall Quality and the default decision instructions. This specifies the
pilot design; a newly generated schedule need not reproduce its exact pairs.
After separate owner authorization, preflight one pair per provider, collect the
primary and reverse work into separate saved runs, and retain their checkpoints.
Inspect completeness, ID mappings, probability validity, binary BT output and
reversal consistency separately. Record date, package commit, requested/reported
models, response IDs, usage and actual cost when available. Keep sample text,
credentials, raw responses and complete returned objects private; publish only
appropriate aggregate summaries. No additional live run is required to use the
dated evidence above.

A future tiny compatibility check can select the two decision profiles in the
existing smoke harness. First inspect the selection without calls:

```text
Rscript inst/scripts/smoke_model_compatibility.R --list=true --mode=live \
  --providers=openai,typesafe \
  --profiles=openai_decisions_default,typesafe_systemone_default
```

Running without `--list=true` additionally requires the explicit billable opt-in shown
above and separate owner approval. This one-pair harness does not reproduce the
20-sample pilot or its reversal analysis.
